la:noun:molestia.html:
mŏlestĭa, ae, f.
molestus
,
trouble, troublesomeness, irksomeness, uneasiness, annoyance, molestation, vexation, disgust, dislike, etc. (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: sine molestiā,; cf.: sine molestiā tuā,without trouble to yourself,: molestiam exhibere,to cause,: habeo etiam illam molestiam, quod, etc.,: fasces habent molestiam,produce, cause,: ex pernicie rei publicae molestiam trahere,to feel troubled,: capere,to be vexed, annoyed,: alicui aspergere,to give, occasion,: afferre,: demere,: molestiis se laxare,: navigandi,.—
In partic., of speech, stiffness, affectation: diligens elegantia sine molestiā,: si nihil habere molestiarum Atticorum est,.—
Transf., concr., that which causes trouble, an annoyance: sermones ne et hic viris sint et domi molestiae,; of spots or blotches on the face: molestiae in facie,.

senses: to put in motion, shake, move
la:verb:molior.html:
mōlĭor, ītus, 4 (
inf. molirier for moliri, ), v. dep. n. and a. [moles].
Neutr.
To set one's self or one's powers in motion, to make exertions, exert one's self, to endeavor, struggle, strive, toil, etc. (rare but class.; syn.: conor, nitor): viden ut misere moliuntur?: agam per me ipse et moliar,: nōsti mores mulierum: Dum moliuntur, dum comuntur, annus est,: horam amplius jam in demoliendo signo permulti homines moliebantur,.—
To set one's self in motion, endeavor to depart, to depart: molientem hinc Hannibalem,: dum naves moliuntur a terra,: in quam (insulam) gladiatores navibus molientes,.—
Act.
To labor upon any thing, exert one's self at or upon, set in motion, work an instrument or engine; to work any thing (cf. ago; class.).
Nihil enim agit (vita deorum), ... nulla opera molitur, : res dura et regni novitas me talia cogant moliri,: validam in vites molire bipennem, to work, i. e. wield, : ancoras, to work, i. e. hoist the anchor, weigh anchor, : agricola incurvo terram molitus aratro,i. e. to work, cultivate, till the ground,; 17; 11, 2, 19: erro molirier arva,: fores, to work, i. e. to force, to break open, ; ; ; : Atharrias ad Philotam missus clausum aditum domus moliebatur,: habenas,to guide,: fulmina molitur dextrā,hurls,: ignem,: opera,to begin work,: aliquid sub divo moliri potest,.—
To set in motion, bestir, rouse, cause to remove, displace (syn.: deicio, deturbo): montes suā sede,displaces,: corpora ex somno moliebantur,aroused,: onera objecta,.—
To build, make, erect, construct (syn.: condo, fundo, construo): muros,to build,: classem,: arcem,: atrium,: aedem,: locum,prepares,: pocula de inimicorum capitibus hominum,to construct, make,.—
Trop., to endeavor to do; to undertake, attempt, set about any thing (cf.: aggredior, apparo): nec ea, quae agunt, molientes cum labore operoso,performing, doing,: viam clipei molita per oras,made its way,: inde datum molitur iter,: jamque alio moliris iter,: viam et gressus,; : animum, to form or acquire for one's self, : laborem,to undertake,: struere et moliri aliquid calamitatis alicui,to try to bring upon,: fortissimis atque optimis civibus periculum moliri,: pestem patriae nefarie,: perniciem rei publicae,: insidias avibus, to lay snares, : crimina et accusatorem,to bring about, find out,: triumphos,: fugam,: moram,to cause, make, occasion,: opem extremam alicui,: dolos apertos,to devise,: bellum in animo,to design, meditate,: Athenienses urbem ex integro condere moliuntur,: mundum efficere moliens deus,attempting,: fallere,: de occupando regno moliens,striving to usurp the government,: nuptias,to bring about,: apud judices oratione molienda sunt amor, odium, etc.,are to be excited, called forth,: tumorem,: vorandi facultatem,: fidem moliri coepit,began to meddle with, disturb,.

la:verb:molio.html:
mōlĭo, īre, 4 (
act. collat. form of molior).
To build, erect (post-Aug.): neque quis quid molit, S. C. ap. .—
In a pass. signif., to set in motion, start: jam sospitatricis deae peculiaris pompa moliebatur,.

la:verb:mollio.gloss: to soften, make soft, make calm, moderate, mitigate, mollify
senses: to soften, make soft, make calm, moderate, mitigate, mollify
la:verb:mollio.html:
mollĭo, īvi and ii, ītum, 4 (mollibat for molliebat, Att. ap. ; :
mollirier for molliri,), v. a.
mollis
, to make soft, pliant, flexible, or supple, to soften (class.).
Lit.: frigoribus durescit umor, et idem vicissim mollitur tepefactus,: lanam trahendo,by spinning,: artus oleo,: dum ferrum molliat ignis,: ceram,: semina,: humum foliis,: glebas,: ventrem,to relax, purge moderately,: duritias,: agri molliti,softened, loosened,.—
Trop.
To soften, moderate, mitigate; to tame, restrain, check; to render easier, lighter, pleasanter, or less disagreeable: Hannibalem juveniliter exsultantem patientiā suā molliebat,: quā mons mollibat mare, broke the violence of the sea, Att. ap. : iras,: impetum,: indocili numero cum grave mollit opus,: poenam,: clivum,to make the ascent of a hill easier,: clivos,: verba usu,: translationem,: fructus feros colendo,to render milder,: caelum,: lacrimae meorum me interdum molliunt,overcome me,: Deus mollivit cor meum,softened,.—
To soften, render effeminate or unmanly: legionem,: animos,: vocem, to make soft or womanish, : puerum,to unman,.

la:adj:molestus.html:
mŏlestus, a, um, adj.
moles
,
troublesome, irksome, grievous, annoying (class.; cf. importunus): abscede hinc, molestus ne sis!: provincia,: operosus ac molestus labor,: alicui odiosum et molestum esse,: tu autem, nisi molestum est, paulisper exsurge,if it will not incommode you,: nihil erit his laboriosius molestiusque provinciae?: arrogantia ingenii atque eloquentiae est multo molestissima,: tunica, a dress of pitch, in which a malefactor was burned (tunicam alimentis ignium et illitam et intextam, ), ; .—
In partic., of speech, labored, affected: simplex in agendo veritas non molesta,: verba,: pronuntiatio gesticulationibus,: dialectos,.—
Transf.
That is done with difficulty, difficult (post-class.): molesta separatio,.—*
Dangerous, injurious: otium, Catulle, tibi molestum est,.—Hence, adv.: mŏlestē.
With trouble or difficulty (class.): moleste fero,I take it ill, it vexes, annoys me,: molestissime fero, quod, etc.,: molestius ferre,: fero,I lament,.—
In a troublesome or offensive manner; of speech, in a labored manner, affectedly: mimice ac moleste,: scribere, August. ap. : moleste uti distinctionibus,.

la:noun:mollitia.html:
mollĭtĭa (mollĭcĭa), ae, f., and mol-lĭtĭes (mollĭcĭes), ēi, f.
mollis
,
movableness, pliability, flexibility, suppleness; softness (class.).
Lit.: mollitia cervicum,: lapidis,: lanae,: carnis,: teneritas et mollitia quaedam,.—
Trop., softness, tenderness, susceptibility; weakness, irresolution; effeminacy, voluptuousness, wantonness (cf.: inertia, desidia): quā mollitiā sum animi ac lenitate, numquam mehercule illius lacrimis ac precibus restitissem,: agilitas mollitiesque naturae,sensitive disposition,: frontis,bashfulness,: animi est ista mollities, non virtus, inopiam paulisper ferre non posse,weakness, irresolution,: Niciae,: inertiā et mollitiā animi,: mollitia socordiaque,: in munditiis, mollitiis deliciisque aetatulam agere,: civitatum mores lapsi ad mollitiam,: mollities luxuriaque,: vocis, Claud. ap. : Maecenas otio ac mollitiis paene ultra feminam fluens,; .—Esp., unchastity, : corporis,.

la:verb:molesto.html:
mŏlesto, 1, v. a.
id.
,
to trouble, annoy, molest: aliquem, Petr. Fragm. ap. ; ; : neminem molestari volo nomine debiti,.—Absol.: uva raro valde molestat,is troublesome,.

la:verb:molo.html:
mŏlo, ŭi, ĭtum, 3, v. a.
mola
,
to grind in a mill.
Lit.: molendum usque in pistrino,: hordeum in subtilem farinam,to grind into fine flour,: tolle molam, et mole farinam,.—Absol.: in mola,: molentes in unum, at one mill or stone, . —
Transf., in mal. part., ; cf. .—Hence, P. a.: mŏlĭ-tus, a, um, ground; as subst.: mŏlĭ-tum, i, n., food made of flour: edo lubentius molitum quam praehibeo a me,.

senses: rock, boulder, cliff, ridge, outcrop, knoll
mass of soldiers, a large army
la:noun:moles.html:
mōles, is, f.
prob. for mog-les; root magh-; cf. magnus; Gr. μόχθος, μογεῖν, μόγις; cf.: μοχλός, molīri, molestus; Germ. Mühe
,
a shapeless, huge, heavy mass, huge bulk.
Lit.
In gen. (poet.): Chaos, rudis indigestaque moles,: vastā se mole moventem Pastorem Polyphemum,: taurus et ipsa mole piger,: stetit aequore moles Pinea,i. e. a fleet of large ships,—
Esp.
A mass, pile, a cliff or ridge of rock: in mole sedens,; .—
A mass or pile of waves: venti, tantas audetis tollere moles,; .—
A huge, massive structure, esp. of stone; a dam, pier, mole; a foundation, etc. (freq. and class.): molem atque aggerem ab utrāque parte litoris jaciebat,: moles oppositae fluctibus,moles,; cf. : aditus insulae muniti mirificis molibus,: exstructa moles opere magnifico, incisaeque litterae, virtutis testes sempiternae,a monument,: moles propinqua nubibus,: insanae substructionum moles,huge buildings, piles,; : sepulcri moles,i. e. a tomb,: molem aggeris ultra venire,.—
A huge engine or machine, used at sieges: velut celsam oppugnat qui molibus urbem,.—
Warlike apparatus, munitions of war: belli,: non alias majore mole concursum,with a greater mass,.—
Trop.
Greatness, might, power, strength, great quantity, heap: moles pugnae,: molem invidiae austinere,; cf.: moles mali,: vis consili expers mole ruit suā, Hor.

C. 3, 4, 65: rerum,: fortunae,: Herculea,: densā ad muros mole feruntur,a vast crowd, immense body,: curarum,multitude, crowd,: tantae corporum moles in fugam consternati sunt,.—

Difficulty, labor, trouble: transveham naves haud magnā mole,without great difficulty,: tantae molis erat Romanam condere gentem,so much labor did it cost,: Corbuloni plus molis adversus ignaviam militum, quam, etc.,.

senses: flour, coarse-ground meal used in sacrifices
la:noun:mola.html:
mŏla, ae, f.
cf. μύλη, μύλος, mill, millstone; μύλαι, grinders, molar-teeth; cf. molaris
,
a millstone; and usu. plur. molae, a mill (driven by slaves, animals, or water): verbera, compedes, molae,: molarum strepitum audire, Enn. ap. (Com. 7 Vahl. p. 153): molae oleariae duro et aspero lapide,: trusatiles,: pumiceae,: aquariae,water-mills,: digni molam versare Nepotis,: versatiles,: mola asinaria,i. e. millstone, too heavy for a man to drive,; : molae olivariae,.—
Transf.
Grits or grains of spelt coarsely ground and mixed with salt (hence called mola salsa), which it was customary to strew on the victims at sacrifices: mola etiam vocatur far tostum, et sale sparsum, quod eo molito hostiae aspergantur, Paul. ex Müll.: sparge molam,: molam et vinum inspergere,: aut molā salsā aut ture comprecari,: molā salsā supplicare,: litare, id. praef. med.: consumpsi salsasque molas et turis acervos,.—
A false conception, moon-calf, mole, ; .—
A jawbone, or the teeth: molas leonum confringet,.

la:adj:mollis.html:
mollis, e, adj.
Gr. μαλακός, ἀμαλός, μῶλυς; cf. βληχρός, perh. Lat. mulier (mollior)
,
easily movable, pliant, flexible, supple; soft, tender, delicate, gentle, mild, pleasant (class.; syn.: tener, facilis, flexibilis, lentus).
Lit.: mollis juncus,: comam mollis ... hyacinthi,: aurum,flexible,: tiliae,: crura,: colla,: bracchia,: cervix,: commissurae,: molle litus,of soft sand,: harena,: aqua,: fraga,: castaneae,: mollissima vina ( = mitissima, lenissima),; cf.: molli mero,; and: molle Calenum,: alvus,relaxed, open bowels,: cibus,mild, not sharp,: ovum,soft,: prata,: gramen,: humus,: lana,: torus,: arcus,slack, unbent, unstrung,: feretrum,made soft by a layer of leaves,: mollissima cera,: mollia panis,the soft part of bread, the crumb,: molles genae,soft, delicate,: capilli,: manus,: latus,: molles Zephyri,soft, gentle,; so, hiems,: aestas,: caelum,; : Euphrates mollior undis,gentler, calmer,: aditus,easy,; so, iter,: via,: fastigium,gentle, not steep,: clivus,: modicis et mollibus clivis,: jugum montis,: trames,.—Prov.: molli bracchio objurgare aliquem, with a gentle arm, i. e. in a forbearing manner, : in molli carne vermes nascuntur,it is the soft flesh that breeds the worms,.— Subst.: mollia, ĭum, n., a kind of fishes, mollusks, .—
Trop.
Tender, delicate, susceptible: mollibus annis,in tender youth,: os molle,easily blushing,: mollissima corda,: mollissimae aures,modest,.—
In a bad sense, soft, effeminate, unmanly, weak (syn. effeminatus): philosophus tam mollis, tam languidus, tam enervatus,: Sabaei,: viri molles, i. e. pathici,; : disciplina,effeminate,: delicatior ... molliorque ratio,: vita,: desine mollium querellarum, : mollis teneraque vox,: educatio,: actio,: Gallorum mens est mollis ac minime resistens ad calamitates perferendas,: sententiae,: si taedio laboris longaeque viae, ut est mollis ad talia gens (Gallorum), dilaberentur,: Romanos molliores facere ad paciscendum,; cf.: sunt qui in rebus contrariis parum sibi constent, voluptatem severissime contemnant, in dolore sint molliores, etc.,: molles in aure fenestrae,.—
Soft, pleasant, mild, easy: orationem mollem teneramque reddidit,soft, pleasant,: mollis et jucunda senectus,: ita eum placidum mollemque reddidi, ut, etc.,calm and gentle,: verba,: mollia jussa,mild, easy,: vincuntur molli pectora dura prece,soft, tender, touching,: sic accensum sed molliora referre jussum dimittit,to return a gentler answer,: saepius molliora respondens,: mollis versus, an elegiac or amatory poem, ; (opp. durus versus, a heroic poem, ): ridere mollia,to smile gently,: cuncta tamen ad imperatorem in mollius relata,in a milder, more favorable light,: pilenta,having a gentle motion,; : mollissima fandi tempora,: hora mollior,more favorable,: signa,: duriora Callon, jam minus rigida Calamis, molliora adhuc supra dictis Myron fecit,more agreeable,: mollis animus et ad accipiendam et ad deponendam offensionem,: in inimicitiis auricula infima mollior, (15), 4.—Subst.: molle, is, n., softness, smoothness: molle atque facetum Vergilio adnuerunt Camenae,.—
Weak, untrustworthy: nihil est tam molle, tam tenerum, tam aut fragile aut flexibile quam voluntas erga nos civium,.—Hence, adv.: mollĭter.
Lit., softly, gently, agreeably (class.): molliter sustine me,: aves nidos mollissime substernunt,: recubans,: ossa cubent,: excudent alii spirantia mollius aera,more easily, agreeably,: cura molliter semina conlocandi,: colles ad orientem molliter devexi,gently, gradually,—
Trop.: quod ferendum est molliter sapienti,calmly, patiently,: abnuere,: delicate et molliter vivere,voluptuously,: aegritudinem pati,sensitively, weakly,: ne quid per metum, mollius consuleretur,too compliantly,: interpretari mollius aliquid,rather mildly, favorably,.
